acceptance_signals: The observer has a narrow injected and Windows-host boundary, performs only read-only enumeration, classifies only relevant process families, and emits no identifiers, raw names, command lines, usernames, executable paths, host paths, or unrelated process data.
Incomplete enumeration, malformed records, ambiguous classification, missing ancestry, unknown task lineage, or snapshot mismatch returns a stable indeterminate result and prevents schema generation.

A fully attributable nonzero ambient baseline is accepted; the exact task root and relevant descendants are tracked transiently, and the existing attribution gate requires no task-owned relevant process to remain.

Deterministic tests cover privacy reduction, classification, ancestry, ambient readiness, same-class replacement, incomplete identity, cleanup, observer failure, command rejection, one-attempt enforcement, bounded JSON discovery, diagnostic reduction, and temporary-directory removal.
Read-only discovery selects exactly one platform-native Windows Codex entry and verifies the experimental JSON schema-generation surface without selecting a script wrapper or daemon command.

After all gates pass, exactly one verified task-owned directory is created under the operating-system temporary root and exactly one schema-generation subcommand is invoked, with no substitution, second generation, or retry.

Generated entries remain bounded to that directory; links, non-JSON entries, excess documents or size, invalid JSON, cross-file ambiguity, and unsupported constructs stop or remain indeterminate without raw values entering retained evidence.

The existing diagnostic returns compatible, incompatible, or indeterminate with bounded counts, normalized fields, stable reason codes, and first-deviation evidence; it does not prove runtime thread or required-MCP readiness.

The exact temporary directory is removed and postflight confirms unchanged configuration, trust, repository state, and ambient attribution with no task-owned relevant process remaining; cleanup failure is not retried.
The two existing upstream modules remain byte-identical; their inclusion classifies current dependency paths but does not authorize behavior changes.

Focused tests, the Python 3.11 full suite, task and repository governance, changed-path classification, JSON parsing, privacy assertions, and diff checks pass or disclose only exact excluded findings.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-95812d33eec34a6790857096ea5c946e and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Build one dependency-free internal Windows process observer and one controlled installed-schema validation driver. The observer transiently reduces only relevant process metadata to normalized class, presence, lineage-completeness, count, and reason-code facts. The driver composes the existing process-attribution gate and schema diagnostic without changing their behavior, permits a complete nonzero ambient baseline, runs at most one installed experimental schema-generation subcommand in one verified temporary directory, diagnoses bounded JSON only in memory, cleans up, reconciles post-state, and stops at the first non-ready or deviating condition. It never starts an App Server daemon, initializes a client, creates a thread, starts MCP, sends a prompt, or requests a model turn.

items: Transient process metadata is sensitive and must remain in memory, be discarded after normalization, and never enter results, exceptions, logs, tests, or repository evidence.
A permissive classifier could mislabel a task-owned process as ambient; incomplete classification or lineage must fail closed.
A malformed installed command could launch a daemon or model path; command construction must be allow-listed and tested before the single invocation.
Generation or cleanup could leave temporary files; cleanup must be registered before invocation and verified afterward.
Generated schema may be large, malformed, multi-document, cross-referenced, or unsupported; bounded discovery must return indeterminate rather than guess.
The one-shot Windows result does not establish cross-host portability, runtime readiness, required-MCP readiness, causal benefit, or user value.
Shared documentation files contain prior uncommitted work that must be preserved.
Excluded changed paths receive no ownership, cleanup, exception, or downstream authority.
Reviewed assumption: Python 3.11 and a read-only Windows process-query surface are available.
Reviewed assumption: The installed Codex distribution still exposes one platform-native entry and the experimental JSON schema-generation surface.
Reviewed assumption: The existing schema diagnostic and process-attribution gate remain importable and suitable for unchanged composition.
Reviewed assumption: The schema-generation subcommand starts no daemon, client initialization, MCP, thread, prompt, or model request.
Reviewed assumption: One task-owned directory can be created and removed under the operating-system temporary root.
Reviewed assumption: A synthetic normalized request is sufficient for static diagnosis without retaining a host path.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the Windows query yields complete ancestry for every relevant process.
Reviewed unknown: Whether installed schema generation passes every gate and completes once.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the installed schema is compatible, incompatible, or structurally indeterminate.
Reviewed unknown: Whether static compatibility would move the remaining failure to required-MCP initialization or another runtime precondition.
Reviewed unknown: Cross-host behavior, causal benefit, return on investment, and real-user value remain unproven.

title: Run installed-schema validation v2 with a bounded process observer
